paper.title: GraphMind: From Operational Traces to Self-Evolving Workflow Automation
paper.central_claim: GraphMind builds action-centric workflow graphs from human operational traces, executes them with multi-agent traversal, and evolves them through Adaptive Traversal Reinforcement (ATR); on 93 held-out production incidents it beats an Agentic Summary-RAG baseline (mitigation reach 98.5% vs 90.9%, hallucination 3.8% vs 22.7%, 4x KQL throughput, 8x less retrieval context), ATR reduces hallucination by 26%, and a 12-week field study shows 97% of scored conversations yield actionable results.

provenance.notes: actual_model/session_id/receipt_ref=null: worker has no access to run receipts; model type per claude-kimi config (haiku slot -> claude-sonnet-5-5[1m]) as stated by controller, not probed.

rationale: 作者报告：轨迹建图在时间留出集上优于摘要RAG；ATR自进化增益小（CI重叠、n=4/条件、评审信号LLM裁判、沉积/评测集分离未述），现场研究无对照。

evidence.quote: We present GraphMind, a system that constructs, executes, and evolves action-centric workflow graphs with minimal human effort.
evidence.support_explanation: Central object: workflow graph (typed Domain/Problem/Action nodes) built from human traces, traversed by agents, and reinforced.

evidence.quote: Third, Adaptive Traversal Reinforcement (ATR) reinforces successful traversal paths, enabling execution-informed graph adaptation.
evidence.support_explanation: The self-evolution component: execution feedback -> reinforcement weights on graph.

evidence.quote: Reinforcement is deposited only when quality reaches threshold
evidence.support_explanation: Retention gate: trajectory quality Q>=0.8; deposit Q/|T| uniformly on every node and edge of the trajectory.

evidence.quote: usefulness is LLM-judged, groundedness measures evidence support, and user feedback, when available, takes precedence
evidence.support_explanation: Reward signal Q is mostly model-judged (usefulness, groundedness); no executable ground truth in the loop.

evidence.quote: Decay removes stale reinforcement, prevents premature convergence, and enables adaptation to infrastructure changes.
evidence.support_explanation: Only forgetting mechanism: multiplicative decay of weights (nodes/edges are not removed).

evidence.quote: when a successful traversal consecutively visits unlinked nodes, a new LEADS_TO edge is synthesized, capturing cross-incident sequences discovered online
evidence.support_explanation: Structural edit retained in graph; synthesized edges are gated only by the same Q>=0.8 trajectory success, no separate validation.

evidence.quote: Although confidence intervals overlap for some individual metrics, improvements are directionally consistent across all four metrics and all four independent runs per condition, indicating a robust signal rather than statistical noise.
evidence.support_explanation: ATR on/off effect is small and the authors rely on direction rather than a test (4 runs per condition).

evidence.quote: this accuracy gain is not free : reinforced traversal explores more paths and executes more actions
evidence.support_explanation: ATR cost disclosed: ~8% higher latency and ~1.5 more investigation rounds.

evidence.quote: 95% CI over 4 runs (2 per method)
evidence.support_explanation: Headline comparison vs Agentic Summary-RAG rests on 2 runs per method over 93 incidents.

evidence.quote: Test incidents are drawn exclusively from tickets filed after this date, ensuring a strict temporal split with no information leakage.
evidence.support_explanation: Graph built from 1,330 incidents before Feb 2026; test incidents after: temporal holdout for the graph store.

evidence.quote: Both systems use the same agentic orchestration loop and benefit from LLM-based preprocessing; the key difference is knowledge representation
evidence.support_explanation: Representation-controlled comparison (graph vs per-incident summaries); not an ATR control.

evidence.quote: two domain experts conducted blind reviews of 19 matched incidents (the maximum feasible due to expert-availability constraints)
evidence.support_explanation: Expert validation small (n=19, 2 reviewers): 4.95 vs 3.68.

evidence.quote: Hallucination Rate , the fraction of conclusions not grounded in executed diagnostic evidence
evidence.support_explanation: Primary quality metric; the grader (LLM vs human) for the 93-incident table is not stated.

evidence.quote: an LLM-judged 1–5 score comparing recommended actions against the human resolution log
evidence.support_explanation: Usefulness is LLM-judged and is also a component of the deposition score Q (Eq. 6): shared judge between evaluation and training signal.

evidence.quote: Notably, evaluation incidents may involve different problem categories than those encountered during deposition, testing whether reinforcement generalizes beyond the deposited paths.
evidence.support_explanation: Authors suggest deposition vs evaluation incidents differ, but which incidents supplied the 90 deposition trajectories and whether they overlap the 163 evaluation incidents is not specified.

evidence.quote: retaining all reinforcement
evidence.support_explanation: Graph-evolution study run with decay rho=0 and alpha=0: decay and exploit/explore parameters are not evaluated.

evidence.quote: After six epochs, 289 new edges are synthesized as traversals discover cross-incident action sequences, growing the total to 20,182.
evidence.support_explanation: Only 6 epochs x 15 trajectories = 90 trajectories; 289 synthesized edges (+1.5%); no accuracy audit of synthesized edges.

evidence.quote: indicating concentration on frequently successful paths while maintaining a long tail of alternatives
evidence.support_explanation: Node Gini 0.60 / edge Gini 0.32 after six epochs: reinforcement concentrates.

evidence.quote: Among the 62 scored conversations, manual outcome classification shows that 26% of conversations
evidence.support_explanation: Field study: 62 of 143 scored; 26% definitive root cause, 71% useful evidence, 3% none; no control arm or pre/post comparison.

evidence.quote: The mean usefulness score is 3.10/5, with 79% rated
evidence.support_explanation: Mean field usefulness 3.10/5 (lower than the 3.49 offline LLM-judged score, different scales/judges).

evidence.quote: coverage gaps (45% of failures): incidents involving recently deployed services or rare failure modes not yet represented in the graph
evidence.support_explanation: Named failure boundary of the store: coverage; telemetry expiry 35%, cross-team 20%.

evidence.quote: A perfect seed graph is difficult to achieve
evidence.support_explanation: Extractor errors remain; ATR is expected to compensate but no experiment tests ATR repairing seed-graph errors.

evidence.quote: we invited domain experts to annotate 30 incident tickets (71 problem nodes, 191 action nodes, 262 edges) as ground truth
evidence.support_explanation: Extraction validated on 30 tickets: node F1 0.93, edge F1 0.92 (RESOLVES 0.86).

evidence.quote: Average cost is $0.22/incident (15.7 LLM calls
evidence.support_explanation: Offline construction cost per incident; median 1.3 min.

evidence.quote: (mean 3.9K vs. 32K tokens per graph load)
evidence.support_explanation: Retrieval-context cost reported (8x less than Agentic Summary-RAG).

evidence.quote: a spreadsheet formula benchmark (124 held-out samples, 6 runs)
evidence.support_explanation: Spreadsheet transfer: 19.1+-1.9 vs 17.2+-1.5 Pass@1 for Trace-RAG: overlapping intervals.

evidence.quote: this comparison therefore measures how well a general-purpose orchestrator utilizes GraphMind’s graph, rather than a controlled baseline comparison
evidence.support_explanation: GHC comparison is explicitly not a controlled baseline.

evidence.quote: treat the knowledge base as static after construction
evidence.support_explanation: Author-stated gap against neighbouring systems (manual artifacts, flat skill libraries, static KBs).

evidence.quote: to our knowledge the first production-deployed system that jointly constructs, executes, and reinforces action-centric workflow graphs from operational traces
evidence.support_explanation: Novelty claim by assertion; Trace2Skill is the only skill-evolution neighbour named; Agent Workflow Memory-style systems are not discussed in the text read.

evidence.quote: applying negative reinforcement to suppress edges along failed trajectories could accelerate convergence
evidence.support_explanation: Failed trajectories not used: no demotion/retirement of harmful edges (open work).

evidence.quote: When new traces arrive, existing cluster representatives are removed and all original members re-enabled (de-clustering).
evidence.support_explanation: Incremental maintenance of the store: global re-clustering on each update; originals kept and disabled (reversible).

evidence.quote: These methods optimize over fixed, well-defined search spaces with clear objective functions; GraphMind adapts the reinforcement-and-decay intuition
evidence.support_explanation: ACO is an analogy, not a reduction with guarantees; the objective (Q) is a model-judged score.

signatures.object: Knowledge store for incident investigation: from per-incident playbooks/summaries to a deduplicated typed workflow graph (Domain/Problem/Action, CAUSES/RESOLVES/LEADS_TO/BELONGS_TO).
signatures.information: Human resolution traces (tickets, text/images/tables converted to text); LLM extractor with schema in prompt; embeddings; no execution feedback at this stage.
signatures.operation: LLM extraction -> canonicalization (regex masking) -> agglomerative clustering with representative nodes -> index update; de-cluster and re-cluster on new traces.
signatures.output: Graph of ~13,344 active nodes / 19,893 edges from 1,330 incidents.
signatures.conditions: Operational domain with abundant expert traces; extractor F1 0.93 on 30 tickets.
signatures.selection_rule: Clustering threshold (0.01 used); no quality gate on extracted nodes beyond pruning stage.
signatures.persistence: Cloud graph DB + vector index; original members disabled not deleted.
signatures.later_use: Bounded m-hop traversal by agents on later incidents.
signatures.claimed_effect: Higher reach, lower hallucination, 8x less context than per-incident summaries.
signatures.failure_boundary: Coverage gaps (45% of field failures), implicit actions, jargon; telemetry expiry.

signatures.object: Reinforcement weights phi on graph nodes/edges and the edge set (synthesized LEADS_TO edges).
signatures.information: Full trajectory (visited nodes/edges/observations); quality score Q from LLM-judged usefulness, groundedness, optional user score.
signatures.operation: If Q>=0.8 deposit Q/|T| on every node/edge in the trajectory; periodic multiplicative decay; synthesize LEADS_TO edges between consecutively visited unlinked nodes.
signatures.output: Updated phi and edges that bias probabilistic subgraph expansion (log-compressed weights, alpha) and annotate planner context.
signatures.conditions: Repeated incident triage where past successful paths predict future ones.
signatures.feedback: Self-judged trajectory quality (no executable ground truth).
signatures.selection_rule: Threshold deposit; no counterfactual credit; failed trajectories ignored.
signatures.selection_data: 90 trajectories (6 epochs x 15) for the evolution study; deposition vs evaluation incident sets not specified.
signatures.persistence: phi stored in graph with decay; edges persist.
signatures.later_use: Next traversals sample edges with probability proportional to [log(1+phi)]^alpha.
signatures.claimed_effect: Hallucination 10.5% -> 7.8% (-26% relative); reach 92.0 -> 93.3; KQL success 15.1 -> 17.2; +8% latency.
signatures.failure_boundary: Over-concentration (Gini), no negative reinforcement, decay untested, small n.

gap.author_gap: Manually authored playbooks/skills are costly, brittle, retrieval-inefficient and miss the long tail; operational traces are underused; existing knowledge bases are static after construction.
gap.checked_gap: The store-format inefficiency (verbose per-incident summaries, 32K vs 3.9K tokens) is concrete and evidenced. The 'static after construction' self-evolution gap is asserted; the paper shows only a small, statistically thin ATR effect and does not test whether ATR repairs seed-graph errors. Neighbours such as Trace2Skill are named but not run; memory-graph/agent-workflow-memory systems are not discussed in the text read.
gap.lineage_closest_adjacent: Process mining -> LLM trace-to-workflow extraction; GraphRAG/Han 2025; Trace2Skill (Ni 2026); agentic RAG (Singh 2025); ACO (Dorigo 1996) for reinforcement-and-decay. Versions as cited; no neighbour full texts in this pack.
gap.residue: Whether execution-time reinforcement adds measurable value over a static graph under proper statistics; credit assignment inside trajectories.
gap.stakes: On-call incident triage across four production database services.
gap.method_response: Action-centric graph with bounded traversal plus ACO-style reinforcement and decay.
gap.remaining_gap: Negative reinforcement, domain-specific channels, coverage growth, validated edge synthesis (acknowledged as future work).
unresolved: Closest self-evolving-workflow neighbours not available as pinned text; novelty claim not verifiable here.

pattern_mapping.operation_correspondence: RS: express the task as conditioning built from retrieved instances. Domain: store experience in a structured substrate and retrieve selectively for reuse. Both = frozen LLM conditioned on a retrieved structured store.
pattern_mapping.necessary_conditions_and_differences: RS card expects training the conditioning channel and category holdout; domain card expects gated writes and store-off certification. GraphMind meets selective retrieval and temporal holdout; lacks store-off and cheaper-baseline runs.

claims.text: GraphMind beats Agentic Summary-RAG on mitigation reach, hallucination, usefulness, KQL throughput with 8x less retrieval context.
